items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: idiot producers who want everything to sound like Wagner or something. I mean that’s the only name they knew you know.

ctx.x: What is it, “One O’clock Jump” is like in D flat or something. I always wondered why — that’s pushing it. The process of learning to do scoring for film, how did you learn to do that, with a click track and all that kind of thing?

I think again by brute force. If you sit there — I sat in the orchestra and watched guys die in front of producers. Good composers. One: Aaron Copland — die in front of these, forgive me, idiot producers who want everything to sound like Wagner or something. I mean that’s the only name they knew you know. They didn’t know Mahler or Bruckner then. Everything was Vaagner—Vaagner—Vaagner. And I think sitting behind the piano bench or sitting behind the piano looking and watching was almost the best teacher. Also, we…
But he didn’t get the joke, he didn’t get the joke, so it was no joke. But I thought of living through those things, and it was a very tough, very tough business.
